title: StyleGAN-style FFN weight modulation versus Mirror and simple controls
hypothesis: On context-conditioned feature-permutation classification, a 4-angle Givens transform of shared FFN weights recovers context-specific teacher behavior with >=1.0 percentage point over native StyleGAN-style input modulation/demodulation at no more than 1.1x its actual payload bytes, and remains competitive with equal-byte FiLM and rank-one residual controls.
mirror_coordinate: four context-specific Givens angles applied as an orthogonal effective-weight view
logical_multiplicity: four context-specific functions from one shared FFN
controls: native per-context input-channel weight modulation plus output-channel demodulation

task.teacher: fixed random two-layer ReLU MLP with context-specific seeded feature permutations

development.selection_metric: mean validation accuracy; ties resolved by lower validation cross entropy

success_gate: On all three fresh worlds, Mirror accuracy exceeds native modulation by >=1.0pp and Mirror bytes <=1.1x native modulation bytes, while Mirror is not dominated by FiLM or rank-one residual at comparable bytes.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the quality/byte gate or a simpler control weakly dominates it on fresh mean accuracy and payload bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism screen only; not a Transformer/LM result.
Fixed-update results are learning-efficiency evidence, not capacity claims.
Effective weight diversity is descriptive and does not itself establish useful logical capacity.
